newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PNG's Highlands Pacific details Ramu/Freida plans.
newsitem.headline: PNG's Highlands Pacific details Ramu/Freida plans.

text.p: Papua New Guinea (PNG) resources group Highlands Pacific Ltd on Monday detailed plans to develop its Ramu nickel/cobalt and Freida River copper/gold projects.

Speaking at the prospectus launch, Highland Pacific's chief executive, Ian Holzberger said a decision on the developement of Ramu was targeted by the the end of 1998 and the company hoped to find a partner for the Freida project by the end of 1997.

Asked about interest in the Freida project, Holzberger said: "We have a number of companies that we would consider suitable that have expressed an interest. A number of parties have signed confidentiality agreements."
Highlands Pacific was born from a restructure proposal put forward by Highlands Gold Ltd after a takeover offer by Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc late last year.

The company said the Freida resource was estimated to contain 4.8 million tonnes of copper and 9.1 million ounces of gold. A pre-feasibility study has estimated project capital costs of US$1.56 billion with an average annual production of 220,000 tonnes of copper cathode and 333,000 ounces of gold in the first 13 years of an expected mine life of 23 years.
Assuming the project was developed in accordance with the pre-feasibility study, production would not start until 2003.
Holzberger said the company would seek to a partner that would fund all of the feasibility study costs for Freida and assist with further project evaluation and possible development.

The Ramu resource was estimated to contain 1.1 million tonnnes of nickel and 0.1 million tonnes of cobalt, the company said. A pre-feasibility study had estimated project capital costs of US$764 million with an average annual production of 33,000 tonnes of nikel metal and 2,800 tonnes of cobalt salt over a total mine life of 20 years.
The company said production from the project could start as early as 2001.
The third prong of the company's strategy was continued exploration in PNG and Indonesia with A$18 million of funds earmarked for this purpose over the next three years.
Highland Pacific earlier said it would offer about 76.5 million shares to investors and institutions as part of its plan to raise A$190 million in a share market float.

The company said five PNG institutions had committed to subscribing for 72.7 million shares. Of the remaining 3.8 million shares, preference would be given to Highland Pacific employees in relation to 500,000 and then to PNG residents.
From the funds raised from the issue Highlands Pacific would pay A$127.7 million to buy the assets from Placer Dome.
Hozlberger said the company would have about A$50 million in the bank after float costs were deducted.
"Ramu takes the lions share of that over the first 18 months with A$17 million being our share of the fesibility study," he said.

The company had allowed A$8 million to fund the development of the Freida project over the next year but would hope to spend only half this amount if it found a partner by the end of this year, Holzberger said.
